description: Capture database changes using Change Data Capture in real-time

datasource_selector.info: Select the data source to monitor for changes

table_selector.info: Select the table to capture changes from

cdc_mode.info:
Choose how to capture data changes:

【Timestamp-Based Mode】(Recommended, Simplest)
How it works: Queries the update time field in records (e.g., updated_at) to find recently updated entries
Advantages: No database configuration needed, ready to use
Requirements: Table must have an update time field (updated_at, modified_at, etc.)
Use case: Recommended for most scenarios

【Trigger-Based Mode】(Requires Database Setup)
How it works: Creates database triggers to automatically log changes to an audit table
Advantages: Can capture delete operations, records detailed change information
Requirements: Must manually create audit table (table_name_audit) and database triggers
Use case: Scenarios requiring complete audit logs

【Log-Based Mode】(Requires External Tools)
How it works: Parses database transaction logs (binlog, WAL, etc.)
Requirements: Requires installation and configuration of CDC tools like Debezium
Use case: Enterprise-level real-time data synchronization

timestamp_column.info:
【Only required for Timestamp-Based mode】

Specify which field in your table stores the last update time of records.

Common column names:
• updated_at - Update time
• modified_at - Modification time
• last_modified - Last modified time
• update_time - Update time

Example: If your companies table has the following structure:
- id (integer)
- name (string)
- updated_at (timestamp) ← This field

Then enter here: updated_at

last_sync_time.info: The last synchronization timestamp, only captures changes after this time. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Leave empty to capture all records from 1970-01-01

errors.audit_table_not_found:
Audit table '{audit_table}' for table '{table}' does not exist. Trigger-based CDC requires an audit table and triggers to be set up in advance.

Please follow these steps:
1. Create audit table: Use CREATE TABLE statement to create '{audit_table}' table with fields like audit_timestamp, operation_type, etc.
2. Create triggers to log changes to the audit table
3. Or switch to 'Timestamp-Based' mode which does not require an audit table
